title: Practice Exam 8
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam. Challenging level.

questions.question: You're following a car at the 3-second distance, but a driver cuts into the gap ahead of you. You should:
choices: Ease off the gas to rebuild a 3-second gap behind the new car
Maintain speed to close the gap again
Tailgate the cut-in driver to discourage them
Brake hard to punish them
questions.explanation: When someone takes your cushion, drop back to re-establish a safe following distance rather than tailgating or braking hard.

questions.question: At night, you should be able to stop within:
choices: The distance lit by your headlights ('overdriving' your lights is dangerous)
Twice the distance your headlights show
Any distance, since reaction is faster at night
The length of the road you remember
questions.explanation: Don't 'overdrive' your headlights—keep a speed low enough to stop within the distance you can see. At night that often means slowing below the daytime limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving at Night

questions.question: The maximum speed limit on a two-lane undivided highway in California, unless otherwise posted, is:
choices: 55 mph
65 mph
70 mph
60 mph
questions.explanation: Unless signs say otherwise, the limit on a two-lane undivided highway is 55 mph. Many freeways allow 65 (or 70 where posted).
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limits

questions.question: You're on a freeway at 65 mph and rain begins. A reasonable response is to:
choices: Reduce speed and increase following distance, turning on low-beam headlights
Keep 65 to maintain traffic flow
Use high beams to see through the rain
Use cruise control to hold a steady speed
questions.explanation: Rain cuts traction and visibility. Slow down, add following distance, and use low beams. Avoid cruise control on wet roads, which can worsen a skid or hydroplane.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving in the Rain

questions.question: A 'speed limit' and a yellow 'advisory speed' on a curve differ in that:
choices: The advisory speed is a recommended safe speed for the curve, not a legal maximum
Both are legally enforceable maximums
The advisory speed is the minimum you must drive
The advisory speed applies only to trucks
questions.explanation: A yellow advisory speed (on a warning sign) recommends a safe speed for the curve or ramp; the black-and-white sign is the enforceable limit. Exceeding the advisory can still break the Basic Speed Law.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Speed Limit vs Advisory Speed

questions.question: You park next to a curb. To be legal, the side of your car must be within 18 inches of the curb and you must also:
choices: Park in the same direction as traffic flow
Park facing oncoming traffic
Leave the engine running
Park at least 3 feet from the curb on hills
questions.explanation: Park within 18 inches of the curb and headed in the direction of traffic. Parking against the flow (facing oncoming traffic) is a violation.

questions.question: A disabled-parking space has a striped (cross-hatched) area beside it. That striped area is:
choices: An access aisle—never park or stop in it
Extra parking when the space is full
A motorcycle parking zone
A loading zone for anyone
questions.explanation: The striped access aisle lets people deploy ramps and wheelchairs. Parking or stopping in it—even briefly—is illegal and heavily fined.

questions.question: Before merging left into the next lane, your shoulder check (head turn) is needed because:
choices: Mirrors leave a blind spot a whole car can hide in
It is legally required to look but not to actually see
Mirrors don't work at night
It signals other drivers
questions.explanation: Even well-adjusted mirrors leave blind spots large enough to hide a car or motorcycle. A quick head turn confirms the lane is truly clear.

questions.question: A 'lane ends, merge left' warning sign means you should:
choices: Adjust speed and merge left smoothly before the lane disappears
Stop where the lane ends
Speed up to pass everyone before merging
Continue onto the shoulder
questions.explanation: Plan ahead: signal, find a gap, and merge left early and smoothly rather than racing to the end of the lane and forcing in.

questions.question: You may cross a double solid yellow line:
choices: Only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side street when it's safe
To pass a slow vehicle
Any time traffic is light
Never, for any reason
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines forbid passing, but you may cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway/street when safe. You may not cross them to pass.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection of equal roads with no cars present, you should still:
choices: Slow down and be ready to yield to any traffic you didn't see
Maintain speed since you have no stop sign
Speed up to clear it quickly
Assume cross traffic will stop
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled intersections require caution. Slow down, look both ways, and be ready to yield—especially to a vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: A funeral procession with lights on is passing through an intersection. You should:
choices: Yield and not cut through the procession, even if your light is green
Drive through gaps in the procession
Proceed because you have the green
Honk to make them hurry
questions.explanation: Yield to a funeral procession and don't break into the line, even on a green light. Let it pass before proceeding.

questions.question: Turning right at a red light, you must yield to:
choices: Pedestrians in the crosswalk and cross traffic, after a complete stop
No one, since right on red is allowed
Only vehicles, not pedestrians
Only pedestrians directly in front of you
questions.explanation: A right turn on red is permitted only after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, and only where not prohibited by a sign.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Right Turn on Red

questions.question: A regulatory sign reads 'NO TURN ON RED' beside a signal. This means:
choices: You may not make the turn on a red light, even after stopping
You may turn after stopping, as usual
It applies only to left turns
You may turn if no pedestrians are present
questions.explanation: This sign cancels the normal right-on-red (or left-on-red) permission. You must wait for the green to turn.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped yellow sign with a bicycle symbol means:
choices: Watch for bicyclists who may be crossing or sharing the road ahead
Bicycles are prohibited ahead
A bike shop is ahead
A bike lane ends
questions.explanation: A yellow bicycle warning sign alerts you to expect bicyclists entering or sharing the roadway. Slow down and watch carefully.

questions.question: A black-on-white rectangular sign reads 'SPEED LIMIT 35.' This number is:
choices: An enforceable legal maximum for ideal conditions
A suggested speed only
The minimum speed required
Advisory and applies only at night
questions.explanation: A black-and-white speed limit sign is a regulatory, enforceable maximum. Yellow signs give advisory (recommended) speeds.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Speed Limit Signs

questions.question: Approaching a crosswalk where a pedestrian waits but you cannot tell if they'll cross, the safe practice is to:
choices: Slow down, make eye contact if possible, and be ready to stop
Maintain speed until they step out
Honk to find out their intention
Swerve around the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Anticipate the pedestrian's move. Slow down and be prepared to stop; making eye contact helps you read whether they intend to cross.

questions.question: When sharing a narrow lane with a bicyclist is unsafe, California law lets the cyclist:
choices: Ride farther from the curb, even near the center of the lane
Ride only on the sidewalk
Ride against traffic
Block the road indefinitely
questions.explanation: A cyclist may move left—even to the center of the lane—when it's too narrow to share or to avoid hazards. Wait for a safe chance to pass with 3 feet.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicyclists' Lane Position

questions.question: A school bus stopped with flashing red lights is on your side of an undivided road. You must stop:
choices: And remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm folds in
Only until the children are off the bus
And may go once you count to ten
Only if you are within 50 feet
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the bus turns off its red flashers and retracts the stop arm—children may still be crossing in front of or behind the bus.

questions.question: Passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights when you were required to stop can result in:
choices: A substantial fine and a point on your driving record
Only a warning
No penalty if no child was hit
A reduced fine if you slowed down
questions.explanation: Illegally passing a stopped school bus carries a heavy fine and a point on your record, because it endangers children crossing the road.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Bus Penalties

questions.question: Driving slowly through a residential area where children are playing, you should:
choices: Watch for balls, toys, and kids between parked cars, and cover the brake
Use the horn continuously
Drive on the wrong side to avoid the curb
Maintain the speed limit no matter what
questions.explanation: Children near play areas are unpredictable. Scan for clues like balls and toys, watch the gaps between parked cars, and be ready to stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Watching for Children

questions.question: Using a GPS app, you realize you need to change the route. The legal way is to:
choices: Use a single voice command, or pull over and stop to edit it
Type the new address while driving slowly
Edit it at a red light
Hold the phone up near the windshield to type
questions.explanation: Operate a mounted device only with one tap/swipe or by voice. To do anything more involved, pull over and stop—editing while driving (even at a light) is prohibited.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cell Phone Laws

questions.question: Which is the best description of why distracted driving is so risky?
choices: It delays your reaction to sudden hazards you don't notice in time
It only matters in heavy traffic
It mostly affects fuel economy
It is risky only for inexperienced drivers
questions.explanation: Distraction means you notice hazards late—or not at all—so you react too slowly to avoid a crash, regardless of experience or traffic level.

questions.question: You're driving with friends who keep handing you things and pointing out sights. To stay safe you should:
choices: Keep your attention on driving and ask them to wait or handle items themselves
Turn to look at whatever they point out
Take each item as offered to be polite
Speed up so the trip ends sooner
questions.explanation: Manage in-car distractions: keep your eyes and mind on driving, and politely ask passengers to wait or handle things so you can focus.

questions.question: A green light at an intersection means go, but you must first:
choices: Make sure the intersection is clear of vehicles and pedestrians
Accelerate hard to clear it
Assume cross traffic has stopped completely
Cover the horn
questions.explanation: Green means proceed only when the way is clear. Late-clearing cars and pedestrians still have the right of way until they finish crossing.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: An intersection has a flashing yellow light for your direction. You should:
choices: Slow down and proceed with caution, yielding as needed
Stop completely as at a stop sign
Treat it as a green and maintain speed
Stop only if cross traffic is present
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow means slow down and proceed carefully. A flashing red means stop, then go when safe.

questions.question: A green arrow and a red ball are lit together: green left arrow, red ball above. You may:
choices: Make the protected left turn the arrow allows, but not go straight
Go straight because part of the signal is green
Turn right on the red ball without stopping
Do nothing until the red ball changes
questions.explanation: The green arrow gives a protected left turn; the red ball still prohibits going straight or turning right (except a normal right-on-red after stopping, if allowed).

questions.question: On the freeway you want to exit but heavy traffic blocks your move to the right. You should:
choices: Continue to the next exit rather than cut across abruptly
Stop and wait for a gap
Cross the gore area to reach the ramp
Force your way across all lanes
questions.explanation: Never make sudden, multi-lane cuts or stop on a freeway. If you can't get over safely, take the next exit and turn around.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Exiting the Freeway

questions.question: Driving in the far-left freeway lane while traffic backs up behind you because you're slower than the flow is:
choices: Improper—slower traffic should keep right except to pass
Required, since the left lane is safest
Fine as long as you're at the speed limit
Allowed for any vehicle
questions.explanation: Keep right except to pass. Lingering in the left lane below the flow of traffic impedes others and can be cited.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Choosing a Lane

questions.question: A freeway sign reads 'EXIT 24 ONLY' over the right lane. If you don't want that exit, you should:
choices: Move out of that lane before it leaves the freeway
Stay in it; 'ONLY' means optional
Stop and decide at the gore point
Straddle the line to keep options open
questions.explanation: An 'ONLY' lane must exit the freeway. If you want to continue, merge left out of it in advance.

questions.question: An adult's BAC of 0.08% means, legally:
choices: They are presumed too impaired to drive and can be charged with DUI
They may drive if they feel fine
They get a warning for a first offense
Only commercial drivers are affected
questions.explanation: At 0.08% an adult is legally presumed impaired and subject to DUI. Commercial drivers (0.04%) and under-21 drivers (0.01%) face stricter limits.

questions.question: Sleeping pills, some allergy medicines, and certain antidepressants share a driving risk because they can:
choices: Cause drowsiness or slowed reactions, leading to a possible DUI
Improve night vision
Have no effect on driving
Only affect drivers over 65
questions.explanation: Many common medications cause drowsiness or slowed reactions. Driving while impaired by them can be a DUI; read labels and avoid driving if affected.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Drugs and Driving

questions.question: The single best way to avoid a DUI is to:
choices: Plan ahead for a sober ride before you drink
Limit yourself to two drinks and drive carefully
Eat a big meal before driving
Wait 20 minutes after your last drink
questions.explanation: Arrange a designated driver, rideshare, or stay over before you start drinking. Don't rely on guesses about how much you can 'handle.'

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with siren on while you're crossing a one-lane bridge. You should:
choices: Continue across, then pull over and stop on the far side
Stop on the bridge immediately
Reverse off the bridge
Speed up and ignore it
questions.explanation: Don't stop where you'd block the emergency vehicle or trap yourself. Clear the bridge first, then pull over and stop.

questions.question: You see flashing red and blue lights of a police car stopped on the right shoulder ahead. The Move Over law requires you to:
choices: Change lanes away from it if safe, or slow down if you cannot
Maintain speed in your lane
Stop in your lane until it leaves
Move over only if an officer is outside the car
questions.explanation: Move over a lane for any stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights; if you can't change lanes safely, slow to a safe speed as you pass.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Move Over, Slow Down Law

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped in the oncoming lanes of a freeway divided by a wide median. On your side you generally:
choices: Continue at a safe speed, staying alert, since a median separates you
Must stop completely
Must move onto the shoulder
Must exit the freeway
questions.explanation: With a dividing median, the Move Over duty applies to traffic on the same side as the stopped vehicle. Stay alert, but you needn't stop for the opposite side.
